reason: S1 changes internal HTML parsing for a DIV nested under a DL in HTML5 mode. H0 already supplies attacker-controlled document bytes through tidyParseBuffer, tidyParseString, and tidyParseFile, so inputs containing the relevant DL/DIV structure can reach both TY_(ParseDefList) and the new TY_(ParseBlock) routing condition. The commit adds no new entry point, API protocol, external state, configuration requirement, or distinct input source that H0 cannot control.
evidence: In TY_(ParseDefList), S1 expands accepted children from DT or DD to DT, DD, or a DIV when TY_(IsHTML5Mode)(doc) is true.
In TY_(ParseBlock), S1 routes nodeIsDIV(element) with nodeIsDL(element->parent) in HTML5 mode to TY_(ParseDefList)(doc, element, mode).
tidy_fuzzer passes the complete fuzz-controlled data buffer to tidyParseBuffer and then invokes tidyCleanAndRepair and tidyRunDiagnostics.
tidy_parse_string_fuzzer and tidy_xml_fuzzer pass fuzz-controlled, NUL-terminated markup to tidyParseString.
tidy_parse_file_fuzzer and tidy_general_fuzzer expose fuzz-controlled file or string content to the parser.
The parser.h change only aligns whitespace in the register_2 declaration and creates no behavioral surface.
recommended_action: No harness maintenance is needed for this commit; retain the existing arbitrary-markup parser targets.
